item.title: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
item.description:
The deep divisions between nations over climate finance, which contributed to the breakdown of COP31 talks, underscored the funding challenges facing African countries as they try to adapt to a warming planet. Although the continent contributes only 4% of global emissions , nine of the 10 most climate-vulnerable countries are in Africa , according to one study. In 2022, the continent received far less than the $190 billion required annually in climate funding, and its biggest economy alone needs more than $15 billion to fully implement climate adaptation policies over the next decade. While South Africa is experiencing heat waves that are damaging agricultural output, its grid remains heavily reliant on the sorts of fossil fuels that contribute the most to global emissions. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
item.description:
COP31 President Murat Kurum speaks during a plenary session at the COP31 UN Climate Summit on Nov. 11, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. —Khalil Hamra—AP COP31 , the United Nations’ annual climate change summit, ended on Sunday without consensus on an overarching climate deal after about two days of overtime in Antalya, Türkiye. The annual conference brings together delegates to shape and formalize an approach to combating the effects of global warming . This year, the main dispute was whether the agreement should explicitly call for a transition away from fossil fuels . That commitment traces back to the Paris Agreement , a 2015 climate treaty that calls for efforts to limit global warming to 1.5°C (2.7°F) above preindustrial levels. item.title: US intelligence chief defends Trump’s comments calling Putin his ‘friend’
item.description:
Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Extremely concerning’: Inside a US Army plan to detonate Iowa lead stores
item.description:
The U.S. Army set off waves of anxiety in Iowa when it confirmed plans to carry out two controlled explosions at an ammunition facility there with just a few days’ notice . According to the Army, dozens of old barrels containing lead azide , an explosive used as a detonator, have become unstable and pose an “ unacceptable risk of accidental detonation .” Intentionally detonating the barrels is considered the best option for controlling the risk, the Army determined. However, the explosions are expected to release a large plume of lead particles, and lead is a neurotoxin. The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is in Middletown, a town of about 360 residents in southeast Iowa. People and farms would be in the path of the plume as the wind blows it for miles. item.title: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite safety concerns
item.description:
Army invokes emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid court order despite worries about health and environment risks The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put on hold plans to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa , saying that continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather starts to turn colder. “To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action,” government lawyers told the eight US circuit court of appeals in a filing late on Saturday. “Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.” Continue reading...

item.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
item.description:
Hackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC), three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating the hack to determine the unauthorized entry point, but, for now, it is unclear what information was compromised, sources said. The NCIC database is a critical information-sharing tool for federal, state and local authorities, helping them track fugitives, monitor registered sex offenders, check whether someone has failed a gun background check, among other information. In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. item.title: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey’s crackdown on opposition and media
item.description:
Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday against a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media, days after police raided Sozcu TV and arrested senior staff. The main opposition Yeni Parti organised the protest after authorities installed a government-appointed trustee at the broadcaster, following similar moves against other independent outlets.
